review_notes: I read the whole file. I compared `LTensor.swapMiddle`, `isoOfInv` and `tensorInvIso` with Mathlib's monoidal and braided API. `swapMiddle` is the same five-step associator/braiding composite as Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorμ`, which is its hom. Mathlib also packages `tensorμ` and `tensorδ` as the `μIso` of the monoidal functor `tensor C`. I did not find a named Mathlib `Iso` form, so the file's named iso wrapper could reasonably stay, but it should be defined from `tensorμ`/`tensorδ`. I grepped the working repo and found a near-identical private `swapMiddle` (and often `isoOfInv`) in about ten other P2M/Sol files. Some of those files use different argument names or assumptions, such as `BraidedCategory` or `A.Modules` specialisations. I did not find a Mathlib lemma that gives `isoOfInv` (uniqueness of one-sided inverses up to iso in a symmetric category), so I did not report it. I also did not report `tensorInvIso`, which is a small composite of Mathlib operations. I did not check whether the P2M/Sol files can import a shared definition without creating cyclic imports.

findings.excerpt: def swapMiddle (X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : C) : (X₁ ⊗ X₂) ⊗ (Y₁ ⊗ Y₂) ≅ (X₁ ⊗ Y₁) ⊗ (X₂ ⊗ Y₂) :=
findings.problem: `swapMiddle` re-implements Mathlib's `tensorμ`/`tensorδ`, the interchange isomorphism (X₁⊗X₂)⊗(Y₁⊗Y₂) ≅ (X₁⊗Y₁)⊗(X₂⊗Y₂) in a braided category. It uses the same chain of `α_`, `β_` and whiskerings as `tensorμ`. Mathlib already has the naturality, unitality and associativity lemmas for `tensorμ` (`tensorμ_natural`, `tensor_associativity`, `tensorμ_tensorδ`). The local copy has none of these, so any proof that needs to rewrite `swapMiddle` has to unfold it. The same definition is also copied into about ten other P2M/Sol files, some with different argument names or typeclass assumptions, so the copies are not definitionally interchangeable.
findings.proposed_change: Define the iso from the Mathlib hom and inverse, keeping the name `swapMiddle`. For example, take `hom := tensorμ X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂`, `inv := tensorδ X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂`, and prove `hom_inv_id` and `inv_hom_id` with `tensorμ_tensorδ` and `tensorδ_tensorμ`. Equivalently, use `(tensor C).μIso (X₁, X₂) (Y₁, Y₂)`. Then move this single definition to a shared utility file and delete the per-file copies. Note that the `calc`-built iso has a different hom from `tensorμ` only up to unfolding, so check any downstream `simp` or `rfl` uses.
findings.benefit: One canonical isomorphism for the interchange map. The existing `tensorμ` naturality and coherence lemmas become usable instead of unfolding a local `calc` term. The repeated copies across files go away.
